title: Pentagon opens UFO files: What happened in Germany in 1944 - Investigations into
excerpt: Pentagon opens UFO files: What happened in Germany in 1944 - Investigations into
content:
Declassified UFO files reveal research into warp drives, stargates, and invisibility technology

A new dimension is added to the discussion surrounding UFOs and UAPs, as the Pentagon released the sixth batch of declassified and historical files, which include documents examining extremely advanced and hitherto hypothetical concepts, such as warp drives, invisibility devices, stargates, and wormholes. The documents originate from the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program and concern a wide range of theoretical technologies, including antigravity, negative mass propulsion, and invisibility. The US Department of Defense, however, clarifies that these are research and informational documents and not proof that these specific technologies are feasible or have been confirmed in practice.

Archives from 1952 to 2025

The declassified files cover incidents and investigations spanning chronologically from 1952 up to 2025. Among the documents are studies examining technologies that until today resemble science fiction rather than operational systems. Among these are theoretical approaches to spacetime warping, faster-than-light travel, concealing objects from sensors, and utilizing unknown or unconventional forms of propulsion. The Pentagon emphasizes that the presence of these topics in the archives does not mean that the US has developed or possesses such technologies.

2010 research on invisibility technology

One of the 2010 files examines early experiments surrounding invisibility cloaking technology. The document describes different methods by which an object could theoretically be made difficult to distinguish or invisible to optical observation or detection systems. Among the methods examined are camouflage, transparency phenomena, and optical techniques that could theoretically bend light around an object. The latter approach refers to the concept of optical cloaking, namely the effort to manipulate light so that an object goes unnoticed by an observer or a sensor.

Wormholes and Stargates for faster-than-light travel

A second document from 2010 examines wormholes and stargates. According to this specific research material, these are hypothetical spacetime structures within the framework of general relativity, which could theoretically offer a way for faster-than-light communication or movement. These are concepts that have occupied theoretical physics and science fiction literature for decades. The fact that they are included in US Department of Defense documents shows that such theoretical scenarios were examined within the context of searching for possible future technological applications. It does not, however, constitute proof that these specific technologies have been constructed or are functional.

Mystery with three engineers and an "anomalous accident"

Of particular interest is a Pentagon research document concerning three healthy antenna engineers who suffered severe symptoms following an incident characterized as an "anomalous accident." Within a period of 72 hours, the three men displayed a series of symptoms, including: a feeling of heat and skin redness, fever, body aches, headaches, numbness, nausea, diarrhea, hair loss, heart palpitations, insomnia, intense anxiety. Two of the three also manifested extreme sensitivity to light and intensely irritated, bright red eyes. One exhibited signs of illness associated with radiation exposure and later developed indications of malignant changes.

Radio frequencies, microwaves, and ultraviolet radiation

The specific document attributed the symptoms to accidental exposure from a close distance to a combination of radio frequencies, microwaves, and ultraviolet radiation. The investigation was characterized as "extensive, but controversial." The case adds yet another special chapter to the declassified archives, as it involves not merely observations of unknown objects, but possible effects of physical factors on humans who were near the exposure source.

New files released through PURSUE

The new batch of documents was released through the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE), according to Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell. Parnell did not reveal the total number of new files nor did he give a detailed description of their contents. He mentioned, however, that the Pentagon and other federal agencies are already working on the next batch of declassified material and that releases will continue. In other words, this specific publication does not mark the end of the process.

From UFOs to a proposal starring a Hollywood actor

Previous release waves had also revealed particularly strange documents. These even included a proposal to NASA involving a well-known Hollywood actor, as well as a 1957 report of a UFO sighting in Germany. The case with the actor dates back to 2001. At that time, Carol Rosin, a space exploration advocate, sent a letter to a NASA official, proposing to bring her husband, actor Jon Cypher, to the official's office in order to promote a space initiative.

Carol Rosin's incredible proposal to NASA

Rosin used Jon Cypher's appearances on the television series "Hill Street Blues" and "Major Dad," his involvement on Broadway in the show "Man of La Mancha," and his ability to sing opera in four languages as arguments for her proposal. At the same time, she cited his love for discussions regarding space as an advantage. Rosin assured the recipient of the letter that the proposal would not cost NASA "a single dime" and that it would require as much time from the official as he desired. She then invited him together with his colleagues for lunch or dinner.

The 1957 FBI report

Among the older documents is also an FBI report from 1957. The case involves an American citizen who had been a prisoner of war in Germany. According to the report, the man claimed that he had seen a UFO while working in Germany in 1944. The testimony was recorded in an FBI document and is now part of the historical material that has been declassified.

The Pentagon reopens the UAP file

The new release brings back into the spotlight one of the most controversial chapters of American defense research. From UFOs and UAPs to the theoretical possibilities of warp drives, wormholes, stargates, and invisibility technology, the files show that the US defense establishment has from time to time examined an impressively broad spectrum of hypothetical technological scenarios. The Pentagon itself, however, sets a clear line: the existence of a research document is not proof that the technology described in it is functional or has been applied operationally. The interest, however, lies in the fact that a significant portion of this material is now moving from closed archives into the public sphere, opening a new chapter in the discussion on UAPs, defense technologies, and the limits of American military research.
